lead.dek: barringinjury converted 70.3 percent of his roster in Week 9, the worst figure in the Cartel, and lost to a 3-6 team by 13.52. He's 4-5 now, and a model that had him at 75.2 percent seven days ago has him at 28.6.
body: THE CARTEL — Seven days ago the front page of this paper belonged to 100 Yards And Runnin, and it belonged to him for doing something decisive. He had traded away a first-round pick of his own, the 2027 one, and brought back D'Andre Swift and Darren Waller for it. The case was that a roster beating 66 of every 99 opponents it could draw had waited long enough to be rescued by arithmetic. Five days later he filed a lineup with Waller on the bench.

Waller scored 23.00. Josh Jacobs, who played the flex slot instead of him, scored 0.50. Swift did start, and gave him 3.10, while Rhamondre Stevenson sat on 13.30. The roster was good for 131.16 points that afternoon and it returned 92.26. That's 70.3 percent, the worst conversion any manager in this league managed in Week 9, and it landed in the one week he couldn't afford it.

Somewhat Goodfellas scored 105.78 and won by 13.52. eloper is 3-6, he's 0.1 percent to play a playoff game, and he spent the afternoon beating a team that had just mortgaged a draft pick to stop losing afternoons exactly like it.

Here's the East as it now reads. Hoya Paranoia is 6-3, 97.3 percent to qualify and 93.4 percent to take the division. 100 Yards And Runnin is 4-5 and 28.6 percent. The other two clubs in there are done — Trade Calculator Guy at 0.1, Too High Safeties at nothing at all — so nobody is chasing him. He's the one chasing, and the men ahead of him keep holding serve.

The luck figure hasn't softened. It reads minus 2.00, still the worst in the Cartel and still the whole argument of his season: 1,284.74 points, sixth of twelve, against a 4-5 record. He's beaten 66 of the 99 opponents he could have drawn, fifth-best in the league. Two of the six teams with a better record than his have beaten fewer.

What the paper can't do any more is tell him to sit still and wait. Back in Week 6 the advice was to sit still, because a minus figure that size usually unwinds without anybody's help. In Week 7 it filed a call saying he qualifies because the luck turns, and that call is still open on the Power Rankings page with 28.6 percent printed next to it. He stopped waiting in Week 8 and this paper applauded him for it. Then he benched the tight end he'd bought.

And none of this is a roster problem. The dynasty board has him third of twelve at 45.65, with 42.58 of that sitting in players rather than picks. What the same board says is that 17.8 percent of that price clears replacement level on current form, Another 31.1 percent of it leans on players the Cartel has put in a lineup no more than twice. He isn't short of anything. He's 210.52 points down on his own bench across nine weeks, the fourth-largest figure in the league, and no trade has ever fixed a lineup card.

One more thing from Sunday, because it belongs beside this. COME AND TAKE IT left 39.14 behind — more than anybody — and started Carson Wentz at minus 2.76 while Shedeur Sanders put up 24.68 in a bench slot. BADS won by 3.14 and sits 7-2. The difference between the two of them isn't judgment. It's that one of them drew the 0-9 team.

notebook.title: Football Morning in the Cartel
intro: There's a kind of arithmetic you do on a Sunday night hoping it comes out differently, and I did some of it this week. Nine weeks in, this league has sorted itself into two piles, and the sorting happened faster than anybody wanted it to. Six teams are 85 percent or better to play a playoff game. Three are at 0.1 percent. Two are at nothing. And one man — barringinjury, 4-5, sixth in points, worst luck figure in the Cartel — is standing on his own in the middle at 28.6 percent, holding a roster the dynasty board ranks third.

That's a strange league shape for Week 10. Usually by now you've got five or six clubs scrapping over the last two spots and a couple of sides quietly deciding they'd rather have the pick. Here the decision got made for nine of the twelve, and it got made in about three weeks.

What I keep coming back to, though, is how much of it was lineup cards. Not injuries, not luck, not the schedule. Twelve managers have left 2,236.26 points on their benches through nine weeks. Three of the four worst conversion rates in the league belong to teams that are finished, and the fourth belongs to Charles Robinson, who is 6-3 and writes about it himself on another page. You can argue cause and effect either way. I don't think it's close.

Nobody quoted here has said a word to me, every trade below is invented, and I am in the standings — five of the twelve 2027 firsts are mine, the dynasty board has me first by 14.92, and I convert less of what I own into Sunday scoring than any team in this league that still has something to play for. Read accordingly.
lede: Something happened on Sunday that this league hasn't had all year, and it isn't on the scoreboard. Five rosters now have nothing to play for. Three sit at 0.1 percent and two are out altogether, and the deadline is five games away in Week 14. That's a market, and until this weekend there wasn't one.

I'll start by eating something. Last Thursday I wrote that nothing whatsoever had moved in the Week 9 window. Two trades had already cleared by the time I filed, both of them Raptor's, and nine claims had been through the wire. The Huddle runs the correction properly tonight. I'd rather own it here in my own words.

So here's what I'm actually watching. The five finished teams are holding $630 of unspent budget between them while three of the six contenders have nothing left at all. Money can't buy a player in this league — it buys waiver wire bodies — and that's precisely the point. What those teams have to sell is men, and what the contenders have to pay with is men. No cash, no cushion, straight swaps.

Three deals below, every price off the desk's Week 4 table, and I've put my own in the middle of them rather than at the end. Two of the three raise both starting elevens, which is rarer than it sounds.

items.head: Five sellers, six buyers with no money, and one man who has to decide which he is
body: Out. Of. Town. Shooters., Trade Calculator Guy and Somewhat Goodfellas are all at 0.1 percent. Lovely Day and Too High Safeties are out. That's five rosters whose only remaining currency is whatever a contender wants off them, and between them they're sitting on $630 of FAAB nobody can spend on anything useful.

The buyers are Cheddar Bobs at 99.2, Chasing Glory at 98.8, BADS at 98.7, Hoya Paranoia at 97.3 and rkobeb2000 at 92.2. Two of those five have a zero in the budget column. So does mine. What that means in practice is that nothing gets bought for money between now and Week 14 — it gets bought with players, which is how you end up overpaying for a tight end.

And then there's barringinjury at 28.6 percent, third on the dynasty board, first in this league at tight end, and 4-5 because he keeps filing the wrong ten. He's the only man in the Cartel who genuinely doesn't know what he is yet. Everybody else found out on Sunday.
items.fit: Playoff probabilities, in order: 99.2, 98.8, 98.7, 97.3, 92.2 and 85.0 for Cheddar Bobs, Chasing Glory, BADS, Hoya Paranoia, rkobeb2000 and the Crew; 28.6 for barringinjury; then 0.1 three times and 0.0 twice. Unspent FAAB among the five finished teams: Somewhat Goodfellas $200, Trade Calculator Guy $199, Out. Of. Town. Shooters. $110, Lovely Day $80, Too High Safeties $41 — $630. Four clubs show a zero: mine, Raptor's, BADS's and barringinjury's.

items.head: The best team in this league is last at tight end, and there is exactly one man worth buying
body: Cheddar Bobs is 7-2, top of the power table and 20.8 percent to win the thing. His tight ends have produced 50.90 points in nine weeks. Eleventh place is 29.40 points better than that. On Sunday he filed Mike Gesicki for 3.10 and won by 44.76, which is how a hole like this survives to November.

In Week 8 this paper filed a call saying he never fixes it, on the grounds that there's nothing in the league to buy. I've been back through the table and I'd soften that to almost nothing. Trey McBride is on a 97.3 percent team. Brock Bowers is on a roster that leads the league at the position. What's left on a selling roster tops out at Juwan Johnson producing 2.51 a week, and Hunter Henry already gives him 2.05.

So it's George Kittle or it's nothing, and Kittle isn't on a seller — he's on barringinjury, starting in a flex slot behind Bowers. That's the whole market. One man, on the one roster that hasn't decided what it is.

deal.label: The deal that makes sense
deal.verdict: TJWill turns a tight end slot producing 2.05 a week into one producing 4.08, and his best eleven gains 0.81. barringinjury gives up the tight end he can't start ahead of Bowers and takes back a back and a receiver into a receiving corps that's filing Malik Nabers at 0.61, so his gains 1.07 — more than Cheddar's does. It's 8.7 percent his way on the table, which is inside what this paper allows me to propose, and both lineups go up. I'd sign it from either chair.

items.fit: Cheddar Bobs: last of twelve at tight end with 50.90 points, 29.40 behind eleventh; Hunter Henry priced 0.97 and producing 2.05 a week; 7-2, 99.2 percent to qualify, 20.8 percent on the title. 100 Yards And Runnin leads the position on 238.10 points and owns Bowers at 3.85 as well as Kittle at 1.93; Nabers priced 0.36 and producing 0.61; 4-5 at 28.6 percent. Kittle produces 4.08 a week above replacement, Kamara 3.27, Quentin Johnston 2.12.

items.head: I've spent nine weeks telling you I own everything and start nothing, so here is me doing something about it
body: 19.3 percent. Of everything on my roster, that is the slice producing above replacement at today's rate, and among the six clubs sitting at 85 percent or better only the 7-2 team in third scores worse on it. I'm first on the dynasty board by 14.92 and seventh on the power table, and I've written that sentence often enough now that it's started to sound like an excuse.

The thing I keep refusing to do is sell a running back. Jeanty, Achane and Judkins are priced at 8.58, 5.25 and 4.45, and I start two of them at best. So I'll pay in the room where I'm genuinely absurd instead. I own five tight ends. I started Sam LaPorta on Sunday for 7.20 and the other four did nothing anywhere.

igross is 3-6 at 0.1 percent with $199 he can't use and a roster that's fifth on the dynasty board precisely because he started rebuilding in September. Courtland Sutton is 30. Travis Etienne is 27. Neither of them is part of anything igross is building, and both of them would start for me this week.

deal.label: The deal I'd make, and I'll print what it costs him
deal.verdict: Four-tenths of one percent apart on the table, which is as close to even as this desk gets. My best eleven gains 3.03 a week — a receiver producing 4.05 and a back producing 4.49 walk straight into slots I'm currently filling with 1.57 and 2.54. His drops 6.43, and I'm printing that rather than hiding it. Back the other way go two tight ends aged 22 and 21, which is the only sort of payment that means anything to a club at 0.1 percent. If he says no he should say no because 6.43 is a lot to hand a rival, not because the price is wrong.

items.fit: Not F*cking Around Crew: 19.3 percent startable at current rates, sixth in the Cartel and fifth among the six clubs at 85 percent or better; first on the dynasty board at 64.15, 14.92 clear; five tight ends, of whom LaPorta produces 1.56 a week; 269.86 points left on the bench this season, the most of any team above 85 percent. Sutton produces 4.05 a week, Etienne 4.49, Loveland 1.01, Sadiq 0.09.

items.head: There's one genuinely good player on a finished roster, and the team that needs him least can pay the most
body: Jaxon Smith-Njigba is priced at 5.92 and producing 9.99 a week above replacement. He is the fourth-dearest asset in this league and he belongs to a team that's 3-6, 0.1 percent to qualify, and has produced 59.00 running back points in nine weeks. Not 59 a game. Fifty-nine, all season, when eleventh place is on 127.40.

What eloper actually needs is bodies at running back and he can't buy them with money, because the only thing $200 of FAAB gets you in November is somebody else's cut. Hoya Paranoia has three backs producing better than 5.50 a week and starts two of them, and jlundblad has filed Keenan Allen at 2.51 in a receiver slot for most of a month.

I want to be careful here, because this is the one where I'd understand a no. Smith-Njigba is 23 and the men coming back are 23, 27 and 26. That's not a rebuild, it's a reshuffle, and a man holding four of the 2028 firsts might reasonably want picks instead. But nobody has picks to give him who also needs a receiver — I checked — and his own board rank is 49.3 percent thin, which means half of what he's told he owns is a guess.

deal.label: The deal that drains the market
deal.verdict: 3.5 percent toward jlundblad on the table and both elevens improve, which is the test this paper sets. Hoya gains 2.76 a week: Smith-Njigba's 9.99 replaces a receiver slot currently worth 2.51. eloper gains 1.05 and, more to the point, finally owns a running back — Irving produces 5.59 a week and the best thing in that room today produces nothing at all. It's the right deal and it's the one I'd least like to see happen, because the only way I meet jlundblad again this year is in a bracket, and I'd rather not meet that version of him.

items.fit: Somewhat Goodfellas: 3-6 at 0.1 percent, last in the league at running back with 59.00 points against 127.40 for eleventh, first at receiver with 443.96; eighth on the dynasty board at 30.14 with 49.3 percent of it thinly evidenced, the highest share in the league; four of the twelve 2028 firsts. Hoya Paranoia: 6-3, a 97.3 percent qualifying chance, and 49.23 for second place on the dynasty board; Jonathan Taylor 12.46, Saquon Barkley 8.86 and Bucky Irving 5.59 a week at running back; Keenan Allen producing 2.51 and filed in a receiver slot in Week 9.

items.head: The 0-9 team had the second-best lineup card in the league on Sunday, and that is not a joke
body: DavisNuaimi converted 94.9 percent of a roster worth 109.60, joint second-best in the league that week, and lost by 3.14. His previous closest defeat this season was by 31.98. He filed Joe Milton in the superflex four days after trading for him and got 13.16, which beat four of the other eleven superflex slots in the league.

Here's the part that matters. He's tenth on the dynasty board, not twelfth, and 7.94 of his 19.93 is draft capital. He's 99.9 percent to finish last, and the 2027 first that comes with finishing last isn't his any more. I own it, along with BADS's and rkobeb2000's, and not one of the five is my own. I'd like to be clear that I think he should keep playing exactly like he did on Sunday, and also that I benefit every single time he doesn't win.

He's got $41 left and two 2027 firsts of his own that aren't the good one. There is no deal here. There's just a manager who's been filing better lineups than three teams above him and has nothing at all to show for it.
items.fit: Too High Safeties: 0-9, 94.9 percent conversion in Week 9 (104.00 of 109.60), joint second-best of the round behind Blame spanos' 95.4; 88.17 points a week and 9-90 against the field; 99.9 percent to finish twelfth; tenth on the dynasty board at 19.93 with 7.94 in picks; $41 of budget left. Joe Milton arrived from Chasing Glory on 5 November and started in the Week 9 superflex for 13.16.

heard: Raptor made two trades in six hours on Wednesday night and started one of the acquisitions four days later. Tre Tucker gave him 7.50 from a receiver slot; Ray Davis scored 0.20 on the bench. He's tenth of twelve at receiver with 230.10 points and first at both quarterback and running back. Two small moves at the position he's actually short in, which is more thought than most of this league has put into anything since the summer.

rkobeb2000 paid $83 for Drew Lock. He's sixth in the league at quarterback with 328.44 points and already owns Burrow, Trevor Lawrence and Tua. jlundblad had $2 in on the same man and it didn't land. I've read that transaction four times and I still can't tell you which of the two of them was being odd.

Nobody in this league started a man the league office had ruled out in Week 9. Seventy-five players carried an Out tag and six were Doubtful, and all twelve of us got that right. Given what this paper has had to print about lineup cards for two months, that deserves a line of its own.

DavisNuaimi put $4 on Audric Estime forty-six minutes after tdsmith23 had already been awarded him for $43. I don't think there's a lesson in that beyond checking the wire before you bid, but $43 for a running back on a roster at 0.1 percent is the sort of thing that only makes sense at four in the morning.

BADS holds not one selection across the next three rookie drafts. Not a first, not a fourth, nothing. He's the only team in this league in that position and he's 7-2 with the best all-play record in the Cartel at 72-27. The dynasty board has him ninth and the power table has him third, which is the widest disagreement on either page. He is the purest win-now roster this league has ever had, and his quarterback slot produced minus 2.76 on Sunday.

My own Week 10 lineup has Ladd McConkey in it. I signed off last week admitting that I was handing out lineup advice with him parked behind Jalen Coker. He's filed. Whether he's still filed on Sunday is a separate question and I'd ask you to judge me on the result rather than the intention.

signoff.label: Last word
signoff.text: Five teams stopped mattering on Sunday afternoon and I own a piece of three of their futures. That's a good week for me and a bad one for the league, and I'm aware those are the same sentence. The thing I'd ask you to hold on to is the 28.6 percent next to barringinjury's name. He's the only manager left with a real choice to make, he's third on the board I write about every week, and he made the aggressive call in Week 8 and then left the man he bought on the bench. Nobody in this league is beaten by their roster. We're all beaten by the ten names we type in on a Saturday.

dynasty_column.byline: By Roy Cowgirl · A current NFL broadcaster · Name withheld at the writer's request
intro: The board hasn't moved at the top and it won't for a while. Charles Robinson is first at 64.15 and that's 14.92 clear of second. He owns five of the twelve 2027 firsts. You don't catch that with a good November.

The number I want you looking at is the one the power table and this table disagree about most. BADS is third on scoring and ninth here. That's a six-place drop and it's the widest gap on the page. He's 7-2 and he owns nothing — no first-round pick in any of the next three drafts, 26.13 of assets and 0.00 in picks. Every other team in this league owns something. He owns a roster and a schedule.

Here's the part I'm obliged to say, because this column keeps telling you where everyone else is soft. 22.8 percent of the total price on this board sits on players the Cartel has started twice or fewer. That's the model guessing. It's not nothing and it's not evidence either.

And it isn't spread evenly. Somewhat Goodfellas is 49.3 percent thin. Out. Of. Town. Shooters. is 45.2. Too High Safeties is 40.4. Those three sit eighth, eleventh and tenth on this board and half of what the model says they own is a projection on a man who hasn't played here. Read those three ranks as a range, not a number.

The opposite end is worth the same attention. Chasing Glory is 7.6 percent thin and Lovely Day 7.2. Whatever those two are worth, they're worth it on evidence. Raptor is seventh here and second on the power table, which tells you he's spent his future on his present. He has 0.36 in draft capital. That's not a criticism. It's a decision, and he made it.

Four teams show 0.00 percent of their price as startable right now. Trade Calculator Guy, Out. Of. Town. Shooters., Too High Safeties and Lovely Day. People read that as a bug every year. It isn't. It means every priced man they own is below replacement level on rate, and all four of them are 3-6 or worse. The board says what it means.

The team I'd buy from is Trade Calculator Guy. Fifth here, ninth on the power table, $199 in the bank, 0.1 percent to play a playoff game. He's got Harold Fannin priced at 4.31 and producing 2.44, which is the softest big number on this page and the same kind of price that put a wrong figure on this paper's front page in Week 7. If you're trading with igross, trade for the players, not the prices.

100 Yards And Runnin is third on this board and he's the one I can't settle. 42.58 in assets, which is real, and 31.1 percent of it thin, which is less so. He's 4-5. He spent his own first-round pick five days before leaving the tight end he bought with it on his bench. There's a version of that man who is dangerous in December and a version who is twelfth on this board next year. Same roster.

The prices here are four weeks old. They say so on the board. Nothing about tight-end scoring or waiver claims since Week 4 is in them, and if that bothers you, it should bother you about every dynasty ranking you've ever read, because most of them don't tell you.

My partner spent the fourth quarter on Monday explaining what a dynasty league is to an audience that has one. Nobody asked. The man beside me is a professional, and I'd like that on the record before I say anything else about him.

draft_column.byline: Mel Kiper Jr. · the board, four drafts deep
intro: Five weeks of 2026 production are in the book and the board has moved, so let me bring you up to date. Four hundred and thirty-two selections across five drafts — 240 in the 2023 startup and 48 apiece in the 2023 rookie draft, 2024, 2025 and 2026 — and every one of them graded on what it has produced in a starting lineup. Not on what I said about it at the time. Not on what the trade calculator says about it this morning.

The order of my board is unchanged and every number underneath it is not. Each of the twelve managers gained between 2.1 and 6.0 points per selection this week, which is what five more weeks of football does to a denominator that has not moved. Chasing Glory stays first at 270.7 points a pick from TWENTY picks — twenty! — and the margin to second place has widened again: 55.8 this morning against 54.4 last week. Make a fifth as many selections as the man at the bottom of this page and average more than double his return, and that is not variance, that is a scout.

Here is the thing I want on the record this week. There are five selections in the history of this league that have produced a thousand points or more, and Sunday added the fifth. Four of the five are quarterbacks and the newest is not. Two of the five are still owned by the man who called the name and three of them are not, and the two that moved — Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes — were the first and second overall selections of the startup. In a superflex league where sixty-seven quarterbacks are rostered for twenty-four weekly slots, that is the whole market in four sentences.

1.note: Twenty selections, eight hits, 270.7 a pick — the best figure on my board by 55.8, and the margin grew again this week. Jahmyr Gibbs at 1.05 of the 2023 rookie draft added 39.20 on Sunday and crossed a thousand points: 1,006.30, fifth-most productive selection this league has ever made and the only member of that group still playing for the manager who drafted him. Jordan Love in the seventh round of the startup, 857.28, and Love has been somebody else's quarterback for a while now. Three of the twenty are still on this roster, which tells you he treats a pick as currency rather than a keepsake. The drafting is elite and the conversion is better.

10.note: Thirty-four selections, fourteen hits, fourteen retained, 214.9 a pick — second on my board and the only manager who manages volume, hit rate and retention all at once. Lamar Jackson at 1.10 of the startup for 1,063.14 is third all-time in this league and he still owns him, which in this format is rarer than the pick itself. C.J. Stroud at 1.04 in the 2023 rookie draft. George Kittle in the EIGHTH round of the startup for 606.00 is the most productive tight end anybody in this league has ever selected and Kittle plays for 100 Yards And Runnin now. The blemish stays Travis Hunter at 1.03 in 2025 on zero, and Sleeper files him at defensive back, which makes it construction rather than evaluation.

6.note: Twenty-five picks, nine hits, 205.6 a selection, third on my board. Josh Allen at 1.02 of the 2023 startup has produced 1,333.70 points, the most productive selection in the history of this league by 219.28 — and Josh Allen plays for 100 Yards And Runnin, while this roster sits eleventh in the league in quarterback production. That is the review in one sentence and it has been for three years. Now the part that is genuinely outstanding: Jeremiyah Love at 1.01 and Carnell Tate at 1.02 in 2026, 47.60 and 38.90, the two most productive picks of a forty-eight-man class, both 21 years old and both still here. Five of twenty-five retained overall. He finds them and he sells them.

7.note: Twenty-six selections, twelve hits, 199.0 a pick, fourth on my board. Joe Burrow at 1.03 of the startup for 727.14 is the anchor and he kept him. Bijan Robinson, who has delivered 93.70 points above replacement in five starts since arriving, was drafted 1.01 of the 2023 rookie draft by Somewhat Goodfellas — the best player on this roster came out of somebody else's board. Four of twenty-six still here, third-lowest retention in the league. And across twenty-six selections I cannot find a tight end worth discussing, which is precisely the slot now costing him a first-round bye.

8.note: Thirty-four picks, ten hits, 196.0 a selection, and that average is carried by two extraordinary swings rather than by breadth. Jalen Hurts at 1.04 of the startup for 1,114.42, second all-time in this league, and he still has him. Baker Mayfield in the TWELFTH round for 888.56 — more than four times what that round returns and the finest value selection this league has produced — and Mayfield now sits behind four other quarterbacks on COME AND TAKE IT's roster. Travis Kelce at 2.17 of the startup for 484.00 is still here too. Twelve of thirty-four retained. Kaleb Johnson at 1.09 in 2025 remains on zero.

11.note: Forty-eight selections, second-most in this league, twenty-four hits — three more than anybody — sixteen retained, 195.3 a pick. The volume is the identity and this week the top end finally spoke: Drake Maye, taken 1.06 in 2024, posted 45.46 on Sunday, the largest individual score anybody has managed in the Cartel this season, and sits on 622.30 for his career. Ashton Jeanty at 1.01 in 2025 is on 249.80 and is the single most valuable asset in this league on the valuation desk's numbers, and he has not been in a lineup for two weeks. Kenyon Sadiq at 1.08 in 2026 is on zero. Seven of the twelve 2027 firsts are in this drawer, so the board is about to double, and volume is already what he has most of.

Ten of fifty-three retained, and no 2027 pick in any round, so the volume stops here as well.

5.note: Thirty-eight selections, twelve hits, 155.8 a pick, and EIGHTEEN still on the roster — the highest retention figure in this league by two, which tells you he believes his own evaluations more than anybody. Bijan Robinson at 1.01 of the 2023 rookie draft for 981.30 and Jaxon Smith-Njigba at 1.06 for 743.76 are both first-rate calls; he traded the first and kept the second, and Smith-Njigba gave him 22.30 on Sunday. Against that: Fernando Mendoza at 1.04, Eli Stowers at 1.10 and Omar Cooper at 1.11 in 2026 are all on zero — three first-rounders, one class, one manager, nothing. Four 2028 firsts are still to come.

4.note: Fifty-six selections, more than anybody in this league, seventeen hits, 155.3 a pick, tenth on my board. Volume has not been kind to him. Marvin Harrison at 1.01 of 2024 is on Not F*cking Around Crew now and has not started a game there; Ty Simpson at 1.09 in 2026 is on zero; twelve of fifty-six are retained. What lifts the grade off the floor is the one room nobody else in this league drafts: Brock Bowers at 1.08 in 2024 for 453.10, still here, 25.00 on Sunday, and the best tight end production in the Cartel at 147.00 — he drafted one half of that room and acquired the other. He also made the pick that produced Sam LaPorta, 2.19 in the 2023 rookie draft, 466.30, who plays for somebody else.

9.note: Twenty-nine picks, nine hits, 150.7 a selection, eleven retained — and he is 5-0, which makes this the weakest board belonging to any contender and a real finding rather than a quibble. Zay Flowers at 1.09 of the 2023 rookie draft has returned 557.00 and is still here; Quentin Johnston at 1.07 of the same draft has returned 102.00. Those are the two ends of one evening's work. He holds four 2027 selections and not one of them is a first or a second, because Not F*cking Around Crew has both. A 5-0 roster assembled almost entirely through trade is a perfectly legitimate way to build in this format. It simply does not grade on my board.

12.note: Thirty-nine picks, eleven hits, 128.3 a selection — last on my board by 22.4 — and thirteen retained. The case for optimism is narrow and genuine: three of the five most productive selections of the 2026 class are his. Denzel Boston at 1.12 on 30.10, Jonah Coleman at 2.13 on 13.30, Jadarian Price at 1.06 on 12.00 — 55.40 points, 36.7% of everything forty-eight picks have produced league-wide. He holds seven 2027 selections and not a first, because that one belongs to Not F*cking Around Crew, and at 0-5 with a 91.9% chance of finishing last it is about to be the most valuable pick in the draft.

board.head: Jahmyr Gibbs is the fifth selection in league history to clear a thousand points, and the first who isn't a quarterback
board.body: 39.20 on Sunday took him to 1,006.30. The group above him: Josh Allen 1,333.70 at 1.02 of the startup, Jalen Hurts 1,114.42 at 1.04, Lamar Jackson 1,063.14 at 1.10, Patrick Mahomes 1,009.50 at 1.01. Three of those four went in the first five picks of the 2023 startup and two of the four have changed hands since — Allen, drafted by Lovely Day and now carrying 100 Yards And Runnin's superflex, and Mahomes, drafted by COME AND TAKE IT and now sitting on an 0-5 roster. Gibbs went 1.05 of the 2023 rookie draft to Chasing Glory and is the only man in the five playing for the manager who picked him.

board.head: Forty-eight picks, 151.0 points, and 141.9 of them belong to two managers
board.body: Jeremiyah Love at 1.01 on 47.60 and Carnell Tate at 1.02 on 38.90 are Lovely Day's. Denzel Boston at 1.12 on 30.10, Jonah Coleman at 2.13 on 13.30 and Jadarian Price at 1.06 on 12.00 are Too High Safeties'. That is 94.0% of a whole rookie class sitting on two rosters the model prices at 0.2% and 0.0%, and the other ten managers have managed 9.10 points from the thirty-seven picks they made between them, of which Antonio Williams, taken 2.14 by 100 Yards And Runnin, accounts for 3.60. Every year in this league the class lands on the teams who needed it least and every year it is treated as bad luck rather than as the draft order working exactly as designed.

board.head: Nine first-rounders are still on nothing, and the 2026 class owns seven of them
board.body: Two are hangovers from 2025: Travis Hunter, taken third overall, whom Sleeper files at defensive back and who therefore cannot score a point in this format, and Kaleb Johnson, ninth overall, who simply has not. The remaining seven are all 2026 — Tyson third, Mendoza fourth, Lemon fifth, Sadiq eighth, Simpson ninth, Stowers tenth, Cooper eleventh. Three of them were Somewhat Goodfellas' calls and two were Out. Of. Town. Shooters'. Seven blanks out of a twelve-man first round in the second week of October is perfectly normal and nobody should be alarmed by it. Seven blanks next October would mean the class never happened.

board.head: The two best tight end selections in league history went in the eighth and twelfth rounds, and neither man kept his
board.body: George Kittle, round 8 of the 2023 startup to Hoya Paranoia, 606.00 points — the most productive tight end anybody in this league has ever drafted. Trey McBride, round 12 of the same draft to Out. Of. Town. Shooters., 605.70. Kittle now plays for 100 Yards And Runnin and McBride for Hoya Paranoia, which is to say the man who found him sold him and then bought the other one. Travis Kelce went 2.17 for 484.00 and sits at 37 on a 1-4 roster. The one top-end tight end in this league still owned by the manager who drafted him is Brock Bowers, 1.08 in 2024. Four hundred and thirty-two selections and that is the list, in a format that pays a premium at the position and in which the two worst rooms belong to teams at 99.8% and 80.4% to make the playoffs.

board.head: The fifth round of the startup still beats the fourth, and the twelfth beats the eleventh by a hundred and twenty-two
board.body: The 2023 startup returns 835.6 a pick in the first round, 617.8 in the second, 491.0 in the third, and then it stops behaving like a draft. The fourth round averages 374.0 and the fifth 411.4. The eighth comes in at 370.1, which is the fourth round again, and the eighteenth at 172.6, which beats the eleventh, the thirteenth and every round that follows it. The eleventh collapses to 81.1 and the twelfth recovers to 203.2, and the reason is two names: Baker Mayfield went to Trade Calculator Guy in that round and Trey McBride went to Out. Of. Town. Shooters. in it. No line can be drawn through any of that. The useful reading is narrower: after the eighth round of a twenty-round startup there is no curve at all, only a scatter with a few live pockets in it, and the two men who reached into those pockets sit fifth and eighth on this page, which is a lesson of its own.

sunday.title: Sunday Brief
sunday.byline: Filed two hours before the early games
lede: Nobody's starting a bye. Just two clubs sit idle this week, Pittsburgh and Tennessee, and twenty-two of their players are rostered across the Cartel with every single one on a bench. Fix This First has nothing to show you, and the injury report's been handled too — four players carrying an Out or Doubtful tag were still filed in starting lineups on the overnight matchup record, and all four are out of them now. BADS moved off Garrett Wilson's concussion to Cooper Kupp, TJWill off Mike Evans' ribs to Quentin Johnston, deucebrat off Treylon Burks' foot to Jordan Watkins, rkobeb2000 off a doubtful Cam Skattebo to Jahan Dotson. That's the whole league reading its own phone on a Sunday morning, which doesn't happen often enough to go unmentioned.

One slot is still broken, and it isn't an injury. Too High Safeties has Elijah Mitchell at the second running back spot, and Philadelphia filed him to the practice squad this week after carrying him active in Weeks 7 and 8. He doesn't dress unless they elevate him, so that's a 0.00 in a lineup already averaging 86.19 a week — the lowest in the league. Isaiah Davis and Jaydon Blue are both sitting on DavisNuaimi's bench on active NFL rosters, and Kaytron Allen practiced in full. It's a two-minute fix and it's the only one the desk can't make for him.

calls.head: Pickens hasn't practiced full all week, and Raptor's in the closest game on the board
calls.body: Chasing Glory against Blame spanos is the tightest pairing this week by three-week form — 143.02 to 136.30, a gap of 6.72 where nothing else is inside 28. George Pickens is Questionable with a hamstring and was limited every day. He's Raptor's leading receiver by volume, 62 targets and 533 yards in eight games, and Chasing Glory sits tenth of twelve in receiver scoring, so there isn't much behind him. There's one thing: Ryan Flournoy, Pickens' own teammate, who's taken 17 targets for 151 yards and two scores over the last three weeks and who absorbs the work if Pickens can't go. In a game this tight you don't guess. Watch the inactives ninety minutes before kickoff and have Flournoy loaded.

calls.head: CharlesRobinson fixed both flexes overnight and left Ashton Jeanty where he was
calls.body: The flexes are better than they were on Thursday. Colston Loveland in for Jalen Coker is the right read under scoring that hands a tight end a bonus on every catch, and Loveland's taken 28 targets for 199 yards and two scores across three weeks. The running back slot didn't move, though. Jonah Coleman has four games, 30 carries and 231 yards. Ashton Jeanty has 108 carries, 37 catches, 713 yards and four scores, he's active, he carries no designation at all on this week's report, and Las Vegas isn't off. Not F*cking Around Crew owns the most valuable roster in the league and ranks ninth of twelve in running back scoring, and this is how both of those stay true at once.

calls.head: jlundblad has a sixty-seven point cushion and nothing to gain from testing a rib
calls.body: Hoya Paranoia draws Out. Of. Town. Shooters., the widest gap on the board — 140.10 against 73.11 on form, with tdsmith23 down to 0.3 percent to qualify. Amon-Ra St. Brown is Questionable with a rib and practiced limited. He's the best receiver jlundblad owns, 76 targets and 580 yards in seven games, and in most weeks you start him without thinking. This isn't most weeks. Khalil Shakir and Keenan Allen both went full in practice, and either of them is enough when you're favored by sixty-seven points of form. If the rib's sore when he wakes up, there's nothing here worth finding out the hard way.

calls.head: deucebrat's second flex pays a tight-end bonus to a receiver
calls.body: Lovely Day starts Jordan Watkins in a flex — six catches for 138 yards in three games — while Oronde Gadsden II sits with 17 catches for 157 yards in seven, eight of those grabs coming in the last two weeks. The slot carries the tight end bonus whichever way it's filled, and only one of these two collects it. deucebrat is eleventh of twelve in receiver scoring and eighth at tight end, and he's a thirty-point underdog to Cheddar Bobs on form, so the argument runs toward the position that scores more per catch. Watkins has the better recent yardage. Gadsden has the bonus and the volume. That's close enough to be worth two minutes before kickoff.

wire.line: Unrostered, and he's taken 19 carries and three catches for 80 yards over the last three weeks. Somewhat Goodfellas hasn't got a healthy running back on the bench at all — CJ Donaldson is Out and Tyjae Spears is both on a bye and inactive — and eloper's waiver budget is still sitting untouched at the full 200.

wire.player: Jameis Winston, QB, New York Giants
wire.line: The only unrostered quarterback who's thrown a pass in the last three weeks, 26 attempts across two games. Too High Safeties is twelfth at the position with 105.06 points in eight weeks, against 163.38 for the team above him. Bryce Young and Joe Milton aren't a superflex plan, and DavisNuaimi still has 41 to spend.

Four catches, 46 yards and two scores in Week 6, and nobody has claimed him in a format that pays a bonus on every tight end catch. Blame spanos is tenth at the position and Trade Calculator Guy ninth; igross hasn't touched 199 of his budget.

watch: Baltimore and Jacksonville are finished. Five lineups already carry points, and Bhayshul Tuten's ankle answered its own question — he played, and he's BADS' 8.2.
eloper has nothing behind Austin Ekeler and Dylan Sampson. One soft-tissue pull in the first quarter and Somewhat Goodfellas finishes the day starting nine.
Four of Trade Calculator Guy's bench players are Pittsburgh or Tennessee, and Cole Kmet's on IR. igross can't cover much today whatever happens.
Jacory Croskey-Merritt has moved to Lovely Day's IR since Thursday, which settles that argument rather more firmly than the desk did.

initial.verdict: Chasing Glory buys back its own 2027 first for Marvin Harrison, a 24-year-old the Crew had just acquired and flipped in three weeks. Getting your own pick back is rarely a bad outcome; paying a young No. 1 receiver for it is the part that will age.
